_about: Money Quest quote series. `verification` must be "verified" before a video can be sent to Buffer; "pending_print_check" means the quotation is consistently attributed by secondary sources but still has to be checked against the printed source. Never change `quote` without re-verifying. `rights` records why the quotation may be used. No quoted author endorses Money Quest.

rejected.quote: An investment in knowledge pays the best interest.
rejected.reason: Not found in Franklin's papers or in any publication before 1818; reference works list it as unverified.
Dweck has said the saying predates her; not presented as her quotation.

rejected.quote: I got my start by giving myself a start.
rejected.reason: Wording differs between sources and the 1917 newspaper source could not be checked.

rejected.quote: Begin with the end in mind.
rejected.reason: Genuine, but the phrase is a registered FranklinCovey trademark; avoided for brand content.

rejected.quote: The illiterate of the 21st century will not be those who cannot read and write, but those who cannot learn, unlearn, and relearn.
rejected.reason: A later composite of two passages in Future Shock; the Gerjuoy sentence Toffler actually quotes is used instead.

quotes.pillar: Financial literacy and healthy money habits
quotes.quote: Beware of little expenses; a small leak will sink a great ship.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.source: Benjamin Franklin, "The Way to Wealth" (Father Abraham's speech, preface to Poor Richard Improved, 1758).
quotes.verification_note: Sentence confirmed in several full-text copies of the 1758 text. Spelling modernised from "Expences".
quotes.takeaway: Small spending choices add up. Children can learn to notice them.
quotes.cta: Try the spending activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Franklin wrote this in 1758, and it still fits a child's pocket money. Small, everyday spending choices are where money habits begin. Noticing them is a skill children can practise.

quotes.quote: I'm not afraid of storms, for I'm learning how to sail my ship.
quotes.author: Louisa May Alcott
quotes.source: Louisa May Alcott, Little Women, Part Second (1869), chapter 44. Spoken by the character Amy.
quotes.verification_note: Wording confirmed against citations of Part II, chapter XLIV (Roberts Brothers edition). Some quote sites shorten it to "learning to sail"; the original has "learning how to sail".
quotes.takeaway: Resilience grows through practice, not perfection.
quotes.cta: Try the Emotion Lab activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Amy says this near the end of Little Women. Resilience isn't the absence of difficulty. It's the growing sense that you can handle it, and children build that sense through small, safe practice.

quotes.pillar: Psychology of learning and child development
quotes.quote: Education … is a process of living and not a preparation for future living.
quotes.author: John Dewey
quotes.source: John Dewey, "My Pedagogic Creed", The School Journal, vol. 54 (16 January 1897), Article I. Full sentence: "I believe that education, therefore, is a process of living and not a preparation for future living."
quotes.verification_note: Confirmed in multiple transcriptions of the 1897 text. The ellipsis marks the omitted word "therefore". The popular version "Education is life itself" is a paraphrase and is not used.
quotes.takeaway: Children learn by doing, one real choice at a time.
quotes.cta: Try a Real Life Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Dewey's point from 1897: learning isn't a rehearsal for later. Children learn when they take part in real things now, like choosing, planning and trying, with support.

quotes.quote: Leadership is not about being in charge. Leadership is about taking care of those in your charge.
quotes.author: Simon Sinek
quotes.source: Simon Sinek, Together Is Better: A Little Book of Inspiration (Portfolio/Penguin, 2016).
quotes.verification_note: Attributed to this book by secondary sources; Sinek says it in slightly different words in talks. Exact wording and page must be checked against the book.
quotes.rights: In copyright. One short sentence quoted with attribution for education and commentary; no endorsement implied.
quotes.takeaway: Leadership begins with caring for the team.
quotes.caption: Leadership isn't a title. For a child it can start with listening to a teammate or sharing a job fairly, and those are things children can practise.

quotes.quote: Nothing in life is as important as you think it is, while you are thinking about it.
quotes.author: Daniel Kahneman
quotes.source: Daniel Kahneman, "Focusing Illusion", Edge.org annual question essay (2011); the idea is developed in Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011), chapter 38.
quotes.verification_note: Wording confirmed from Kahneman's own Edge essay. The book's chapter 38 wording should be checked if the book is cited alone.
quotes.rights: In copyright. One short sentence quoted with attribution for education and commentary; no endorsement implied.
quotes.takeaway: A short pause helps children choose with care.
quotes.cta: Try the Brain Lab activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: In the moment, the thing a child wants can feel like the only thing that matters. Adults feel it too. A short pause before deciding is a habit worth practising together.

quotes.quote: Innovation is the specific instrument of entrepreneurship.
quotes.author: Peter F. Drucker
quotes.source: Peter F. Drucker, Innovation and Entrepreneurship: Practice and Principles (Harper & Row, 1985).
quotes.verification_note: Wording consistent across secondary sources; chapter and page not confirmed.
quotes.rights: In copyright. One short sentence quoted with attribution for education and commentary; no endorsement implied.
quotes.takeaway: Every new idea starts with a problem worth solving.
quotes.cta: Build a first business idea in Entrepreneur Quest.
quotes.caption: Entrepreneurship for children isn't about making money. It's about noticing a problem and trying an idea, and learning from what happens next.

quotes.quote: Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: Epictetus, Enchiridion, section 5, translated by George Long (1877).
quotes.verification_note: Matches versions described as Long's translation; exact wording must be checked against Long's text.
quotes.takeaway: Children can learn to notice a feeling before they act.
quotes.cta: Explore feelings in the Emotion Lab.
quotes.caption: An idea almost two thousand years old: what we tell ourselves about an event shapes how it feels. Children can learn to notice a feeling and choose a next step.

quotes.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get.
quotes.author: Benjamin Graham
quotes.source_line: as quoted by Warren Buffett, 2008 shareholder letter
quotes.source: Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter for 2008, attributing the line to Benjamin Graham.
quotes.verification_note: Secondary sources confirm the line is in the 2008 letter; exact wording must be checked against the letter PDF.
quotes.rights: In copyright. One short sentence quoted with attribution for education and commentary; no endorsement implied.
quotes.takeaway: Children can learn to ask what something is really worth.
quotes.cta: Practise smart choices in Market Town.
quotes.caption: A bigger box or a brighter label isn't always the better choice. Asking "what am I really getting?" is a question children can practise on every shopping trip.

quotes.quote: Tomorrow's illiterate will not be the man who can't read; he will be the man who has not learned how to learn.
quotes.author: Herbert Gerjuoy
quotes.source_line: quoted in Alvin Toffler, Future Shock, 1970
quotes.source: Psychologist Herbert Gerjuoy, quoted by Alvin Toffler in Future Shock (1970), chapter 18.
quotes.verification_note: Secondary sources agree Toffler is quoting Gerjuoy (p. 414, Bantam edition). The popular "learn, unlearn and relearn" version credited to Toffler is a later composite and is not used. Check wording against the book.
quotes.rights: In copyright. One short sentence quoted with attribution for education and commentary; no endorsement implied.
quotes.takeaway: Learning how to learn is a skill for life.
quotes.caption: This line is usually credited to Alvin Toffler. He was quoting psychologist Herbert Gerjuoy. Either way the point stands: knowing how to learn matters as much as what you know.

quotes.pillar: Financial literacy and healthy money habits
quotes.quote: Every action you take is a vote for the type of person you wish to become.
quotes.author: James Clear
quotes.verification_note: Confirmed on the author's own site, which publishes the chapter 2 excerpt and repeats the sentence.
quotes.rights: In copyright. One short sentence quoted with attribution for education and commentary; no endorsement implied.
quotes.cta: Try the saving activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: A coin in a jar is a small thing. Repeated every week, it becomes evidence a child can point to: "I'm someone who saves."

quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.source: Benjamin Franklin, "The Way to Wealth" (1758), quoting his earlier Poor Richard's Almanack.
quotes.verification_note: Confirmed in full-text copies of the 1758 text. The year of its first almanac appearance is not confirmed, so only 1758 is cited.
quotes.takeaway: Small savings, repeated, reach big goals.
quotes.cta: Set a savings goal on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: One small step doesn't look like much. Franklin's point is that many of them do the work. A savings goal lets a child see that for themselves.

quotes.pillar: Psychology of learning and child development
quotes.quote: What the child is able to do in collaboration today he will be able to do independently tomorrow.
quotes.author: Lev Vygotsky
quotes.source: L. S. Vygotsky, Thinking and Speech (1934), in The Collected Works of L. S. Vygotsky, vol. 1 (Plenum, 1987), p. 211, trans. Norris Minick.
quotes.verification_note: Cited with this page by several academic secondary sources; translations differ, so wording must be checked against the 1987 edition.
quotes.rights: In copyright. One short sentence quoted with attribution for education and commentary; no endorsement implied.
quotes.cta: Try a Real Life Quest together.
quotes.caption: Doing something alongside a child isn't doing it for them. Shared practice now is how independent skill gets built.

quotes.quote: Self-belief does not necessarily ensure success, but self-disbelief assuredly spawns failure.
quotes.author: Albert Bandura
quotes.source: Albert Bandura, Self-Efficacy: The Exercise of Control (W. H. Freeman, 1997).
quotes.verification_note: Attributed to this book by secondary sources; page not confirmed.
quotes.rights: In copyright. One short sentence quoted with attribution for education and commentary; no endorsement implied.
quotes.takeaway: Confidence grows when children see themselves succeed.
quotes.cta: Let children practise with low-stakes choices.
quotes.caption: Bandura studied how belief in our own ability affects what we attempt. For children, that belief is built from small, real successes, in settings where mistakes cost nothing.

quotes.quote: The greatest sign of success for a teacher is to be able to say, "The children are now working as if I did not exist."
quotes.author: Maria Montessori
quotes.source: Maria Montessori, The Absorbent Mind (1949), chapter 27, "The Teacher's Preparation" (trans. Claude A. Claremont).
quotes.verification_note: Cited to chapter 27, p. 283 by Montessori organisations; wording varies between translations and must be checked against the edition cited.
quotes.rights: In copyright. One short sentence quoted with attribution for education and commentary; no endorsement implied.
quotes.takeaway: Independence is built one small responsibility at a time.
quotes.caption: Montessori measured a teacher's success by how little the children needed her. The same idea works at home: give one small responsibility, then step back.

quotes.quote: The only way to have a friend is to be one.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.verification_note: Widely cited to this essay; the sentence was not confirmed against the essay text in this research pass.
quotes.takeaway: Kindness and friendship are skills children can practise.
quotes.caption: Friendship is something children do, not something they get. Listening, sharing and giving are skills, and they improve with practice.
